scores.claim_text: As of December 31, 2025, Serve's fleet consisted of over 2,000 sidewalk delivery robots.
supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee returned 7 applications / 2 granted patents for 'Serve Robotics', including DELIVERY ROBOT and SELF SANITIZING STORAGE OF A DELIVERY ROBOT — consistent with a real delivery-robot R&D effort, but the patent footprint is small relative to a 2,000-unit claim.
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee: n_granted=2, n_total_applications=7; category 'robot' hits=4. Filing also discloses FY2025 revenue of only $2.7M against the 2,000-robot fleet claim — ARPU per robot ~$1,350/year, which implies very low utilization vs the headline fleet number. No M-source directly counts deployed sidewalk robots.
scores.interpretation: STAGE LADDER applied (Heuristic 3). Headline 'over 2,000 robots' is a fleet/inventory figure not a commercial-deployment figure. $2.7M revenue across 2,000+ robots = ~$1,350/robot/year — clearly inconsistent with commercial utilization. Either fleet is heavily idle / inventory-staged, or many robots are not yet revenue-producing. Pilot-vs-commercial conflation per Heuristic 9. Scored MODERATE because the fleet number itself is plausible (filing-stated) but is being marketed as an operational figure when revenue per robot betrays minimal utilization.

scores.claim_text: Serve maintains platform-level integrations with food delivery platforms, such as Uber Eats and DoorDash, that enable real-time order dispatch and operational coordination.
supports: edgar_fts cik=Uber (0001543151) search 'Serve Robotics': total_hits=1 — a single Q4-2021 earnings press-release 8-K (2022-02-09). NO mention in any Uber 10-K, 10-Q, or DEF 14A through cutoff.
scores.M_check: Counterparty-disclosure cross-check per Layer 3 Rule 7. Uber Eats is positioned as the centerpiece partnership and counts for the majority of revenue via Customer A (37%) / Customer B (18%) profile, but the counterparty has effectively zero disclosure footprint.
scores.interpretation: Hard counterparty-asymmetry signal. Uber's 10-K does not name Serve as a material partner/customer at any point — only a 2022 earnings-press-release tag-out. For Uber, the Serve relationship is immaterial (which is consistent with Uber's scale — ~$45B revenue), but on the SERV side this relationship is the entire business thesis. Heuristic 7 says ABSENCE for a pilot-stage relationship = MODERATE; ABSENCE while company claims headline customer revenue = RED. Here SERV concentrates 37% of revenue in 'Customer A' (most plausibly Uber Eats) — that IS headline customer revenue. Rating SEVERE rather than RED because Uber's scale legitimately excuses non-disclosure (Serve is too small to be material to Uber) — but the asymmetry still indicates the relationship has not graduated past pilot/limited-deployment status, contradicting the framing in SERV's filing.

scores.claim_text: For FY2025, Customer A represented 37% and Customer B represented 18% of total revenues; combined ~55% from two unnamed customers (likely Uber Eats and DoorDash).
supports: Customer concentration disclosed in SERV's own 10-K (Customer A 37%, Customer B 18% in 2025; Customer A 26%, Customer B 65% in 2024) — note dramatic shift: Customer B went from 65% to 18% — a >70% YoY decline in proportional revenue from that customer, while total revenue grew only 46%. Implies Customer B revenue declined meaningfully in absolute terms.
Neither customer is named in the 10-K (Heuristic 9: name-variant fragility but here the company itself withholds the name).
Counterparty disclosure on Uber side = single 2022 8-K only; DoorDash side = zero.
scores.M_check: Cross-checked SERV's own 10-K disclosure against Uber/DoorDash counterparty filings via edgar_fts. SERV chose Customer A/B/C/D/E pseudonymization rather than naming the counterparty, despite the partner relationship being central to the equity story.
scores.interpretation: Two concerning sub-signals: (1) Customer B's share collapsed from 65% to 18% YoY — and since total revenue only grew 46% ($1.8M → $2.7M), Customer B's absolute revenue dropped from ~$1.18M to ~$0.48M, a ~60% decline. That looks like a major customer churn or pilot wind-down. (2) Refusal to name partners despite marketing the Uber Eats / DoorDash relationships in MD&A and risk factors is a soft-but-real red flag. Scored MODERATE because the disclosure is technically compliant and the customer churn is acknowledged via the customer-concentration table itself.

scores.claim_text: Serve generated $2.7 million in revenue for FY2025 (vs $1.8M in FY2024) against a net loss of $101.4 million and accumulated deficit of $208.9 million.
supports: Direct disclosure in 10-K MD&A. Revenue $2.65M, cost of revenue $18.0M (gross loss $15.4M — i.e. gross margin of NEGATIVE 580%), opex $97.4M, net loss $101.4M.
Cash burn from ops $80.2M in FY2025 alone, accumulated deficit $208.9M.
Subsequent capital raises: $80M (Jan 2025) and $100M (Oct 2025), plus stock-funded M&A — clear distress-adjacent funding cadence.
scores.M_check: Internal financials only — no external M-source needed for arithmetic. The headline is staggering: gross margin is negative 580% (cost to provide $1 of delivery service is $6.80). Combined with the disclosed material weaknesses in ICFR (see C5), this is a Heuristic 10 distress fingerprint.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 10 + Heuristic 11. The company is generating $2.7M of revenue against $101M of annual losses (revenue is 2.6% of losses), with deeply-negative gross margins indicating the unit economics of robotic delivery do NOT work at current scale. Note the company's three acquisitions (Voysys Apr-25, Vayu Aug-25, Diligent Jan-26, Vebu Feb-26) and capital raises are stretching capital ahead of any commercial-revenue inflection. Scored RED because (a) gross margin is negative-multiple-hundred-percent and (b) growth pattern is acquisitive-cash-burning with no demonstrated unit economics at scale, not a Heuristic 4 'investment-led equity round' that comes with a customer commitment.

scores.claim_text: Management concluded disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting were not effective as of Dec 31, 2025 due to multiple material weaknesses (segregation of duties, control environment, comprehensive accounts and disclosures).
supports: Item 9A of the 10-K explicitly states 'our principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective.' Multiple distinct material weaknesses enumerated (control environment, segregation of duties, controls over substantially all accounts and disclosures).
Acknowledgement of 'comprehensive' deficiencies covering essentially all financial reporting areas.
scores.M_check: Self-disclosure. This is a serious, broad, multi-area failure — not a narrow technical material weakness. It explicitly admits the company lacks the size/resources for effective controls. Particularly notable given the company completed FOUR acquisitions (Voysys, Vayu, Diligent, Vebu) in a 10-month window across 2025–early 2026, each requiring complex purchase-price allocation, and acknowledges that Diligent and Vebu accounting is incomplete at filing.

weaknesses_disclosed: controls over substantially all accounts and disclosures

scores.interpretation: Broad-scope material weakness in a company actively executing serial M&A is a Heuristic 10 distress fingerprint and elevates the reliability risk of all other financial claims in this filing (including the customer concentration table and revenue disclosure). Scored RED because the weaknesses are not narrow / remediated — they cover 'substantially all accounts and disclosures' which is essentially a blanket admission.

scores.claim_text: On January 27, 2026 Serve completed the acquisition of Diligent Robotics Inc. (Moxi healthcare robots) for ~$29M, extending the platform to hospitals and citing 'established commercial relationships with healthcare systems and institutions.'
supports: uspto_odp shows Diligent Robotics has 6 granted patents and 23 total applications, all in robotic learning / navigation / manipulation / multi-sensor perception domains (category 'autonomy' hits=21). The IP is real and tech-relevant to indoor hospital robotics.

However, the 10-K does not name ANY healthcare-system customer of Diligent (no specific hospital networks, no Joint Commission certifications named, no contract values disclosed), and the 'established commercial relationships' claim is presented as a forward-looking expectation rather than a current revenue figure.
Acquisition accounting is explicitly 'incomplete' at 10-K filing date — Serve has not yet assigned purchase-price values.
scores.M_check: USPTO confirmed Diligent's IP depth (Heuristic 8 PASS-equivalent on patents). Counterparty-disclosure check NOT performed because no specific health-system customers are named (no anchor to look up). The cohort prompt warns 'pilots-as-PR is the central evasion pattern' — the 'established commercial relationships with healthcare systems and institutions' language is exactly the kind of qualitative, unverifiable claim that Heuristic 9 flags.
scores.interpretation: Patent footprint validates Diligent's technology bona-fides. The 'established commercial relationships' phrasing without naming any specific health system or disclosing the inherited revenue base earns a MODERATE rating. The fact that the acquisition closed only ~6 weeks before 10-K filing and PPA is incomplete prevents a more aggressive call but also prevents the company from substantiating the 'scalable, recurring revenue growth' narrative — Heuristic 3 stage ladder is clearly being skipped. The pivot from sidewalk delivery to a second vertical (healthcare) plus a third (Vebu food tech) within months is a classic 'shopping for a thesis' pattern when the core business is not scaling.

scores.claim_text: Company raised $80M in January 2025 registered direct offering at $19/share and another $100M in October 2025 at $16/share (Nvidia-led financing per cohort metadata).
supports: Registered direct offerings disclosed directly in 10-K Recent Developments section (Jan 7 2025: 4,210,525 shares @ $19, $80M gross; Oct 10 2025: 6,250,000 shares @ $16, $100M gross). Both raises are factually documented.
edgar_fts cik=Nvidia (0001045810) search 'Serve Robotics': total_hits=0. Nvidia does NOT disclose a Serve investment in any 10-K, 10-Q, or 8-K.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts cik=Nvidia: zero hits. Cohort metadata flags this as 'Nvidia-led' but neither the 10-K text quoted nor Nvidia's own filings name Nvidia as the participating investor. The financings are described as 'with certain institutional investors' without naming them. CANNOT VERIFY the Nvidia-led characterization from public filings.
scores.interpretation: Per Heuristic 4, Nvidia-led financings are equity investments, not customer revenue — they do not validate commercial traction. The raises themselves are real and disclosed, but the 'Nvidia-led' attribution cannot be verified from EDGAR fulltext. Additionally, the down-round-like share price progression ($19 → $16, ~16% decline within 9 months despite the company adding $100M of cash and announcing healthcare expansion) is a soft negative on investor demand. Scored UNVERIFIABLE on the Nvidia-leadership attribution specifically; the dollar amounts are PASS on disclosure terms.
